speaker: Kimi K3
text: CUB's latest quarter shows revenue up 32% year-over-year and net income jumping to 4.16B from 3.32B a year ago, so the 7.4% EPS beat wasn't a fluke — it's backed by real top-line momentum. The stock's only 4.9% off its all-time high with a 5-year CAGR of 13.4%, which is respectable but won't get you to 10x on its own; you'd need roughly 18 years at that pace before taxes and costs. For the Rs 10,000 India sleeve, CUB fits as a quality compounder, but the 10x goal still demands either a multi-bagger pick or a much longer horizon. On your IPO question: with $10 you can't participate in US IPOs (minimums are typically hundreds of shares), and in India the minimum application size is usually Rs 15,000, so your Rs 10,000 budget only works for secondary-market buys. Buying Reliance on Zerodha delivery would cost you about Rs 38 round-trip on Rs 10,000 (0.38%), plus 20% short-term capital gains tax if sold within a year.
